transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-04
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Leo (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SRE), Rajiv (Aurelia ML), Elena (Aurelia Infra), Tom (Aurelia ML), Sofia (Aurelia Security)
Shared artifacts: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/hybrid-profiling-2026 (deck), https://redwood.app/sheets/hybrid-int8-awq-raw (spreadsheet)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough): discussed mixed-precision fallback, KV cache staleness during scale events, and layer-sensitivity. Agreed to run microbench and provide sample prompts.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, want to do quick intros and then go straight into the regression traces you sent us, is that ok?
[00:12] Rajiv: yep sounds good, sorry we're on a bit of a tight timeline, our compliance window next month.
[00:18] Leo: no problem, we'll focus on root cause candidates: quantization artifacts (int8/gptq/awq), runtime fallback behavior, and KV cache effects when replicas scale.
[00:28] Elena: quick note - our infra has episodes of autoscale spikes, which is when the bad outputs showed up in prod, so that's important.
[00:36] Tom: yeah we saw short spans where NER entity labels dropped confidence and occasionally hallucinated, not massive but enough to fail our QA asserts.
[00:47] Priya: logs you sent show drop coincident with pod churn and a cache miss storm - might be KV cache staleness but need to confirm.

[01:05] Speaker 1 (customer?): so first question, what's the delta between doing pure int8 GPTQ and AWQ on our checkpoint? we ran both and AWQ seemed a little worse on hallucinations.
[01:19] Leo: short answer: AWQ's stochastic weight quantization can change small logits distribution; in many LLMs AWQ retains perplexity well but for clinical NER rare tokens and punctuation can shift. GPTQ tends to be more deterministic per-layer but larger memory.
[01:34] Rajiv: when you say "shift" do you mean tokenization-level or attention scoring?
[01:40] Leo: mostly attention logits, small shifts amplified by softmax on low-entropy sequences, so predictions for boundary tokens can flip. we saw this in your regression trace at 12:23 in the spreadsheet where the punctuation token probability dropped by ~0.07.

[02:10] Elena: and how does FP8 play into this? we have A100s that can do FP8, would that be safer?
[02:18] Maya: FP8 can recover some dynamic range but it's hardware-dependent and not universal across customer's clouds/on-prem GPUs. also FP8 can cost more in throughput vs int8.
[02:27] Leo: for your dataset FP8 reduced the NER flips in our dev runs by about 60% vs AWQ; but latency increased ~12% under our batching config.

[03:02] Tom: right now we're budget-constrained; if FP8 costs too much we need fallback logic that keeps latency/SLOs and avoids bad outputs. what does Redwood recommend?
[03:12] Priya: we usually do a hybrid approach: quantize layers that are insensitive to accuracy to int8/AWQ and keep sensitivity-critical layers in higher precision (FP16 or FP8). Redwood has tooling to run per-layer sensitivity scans.
[03:26] Rajiv: can you explain sensitivity scan? how long does it run on our model?
[03:30] Leo: depends on model size; for your 13B model we can run a coarse-scan (10-20 prompts per layer) in about 2 hours on a single GPU, full scan maybe 6-8 hours. we prioritize top-k attention layers and LM heads.

[04:05] Speaker 2 (maybe Maya): ok let's pivot to the KV cache issue — you said there were staleness windows during scale down, can you walk us through timeline?
[04:14] Rajiv: yes at 11:40 UTC we dropped from 8 to 5 pods in a few seconds (HPA overshoot) and at that same time our request tail latency spiked and the QA alert fired.
[04:24] Elena: we saw a burst of cache evictions then a rehydration storm — some requests got older KV entries which led to inconsistent context for streaming chat responses.
[04:35] Leo: that matches a class of bugs where KV pointers are not re-mapped atomically during seamless handoff; Redwood's runtime has sticky-KV routing options and a coherence mode, but it trades off memory and cross-pod traffic.
[04:50] Priya: we recommended enabling the KV sticky + short TTLs for your workload as a compromise — reduces cross-pod rehydration at scale events.

[05:20] Tom: what's cost impact of sticky-KV?
[05:24] Leo: with sticky-KV you'll need slightly more reserved memory per pod, and if you keep a moderately long TTL you can avoid repeated recompute at cost of more RAM; we can quantify in the benchmark sheet.
[05:35] Rajiv: can the runtime fallback to smaller model variant automatically if we detect a regression? e.g., if int8 path fails check, fall back to FP16 host?
[05:44] Maya: yes Redwood supports policy-driven fallback: route by latency or quality flags. you can set a canary that checks a subset of responses against baseline prompts and fallback when delta threshold surpassed.
[05:55] Elena: is that reactive or proactive? we need deterministic behavior for audits.
[05:59] Leo: both; the canary is proactive periodic sampling, and there is reactive fallback on detection of metric drift. you can tie it to audit logs via our console.

[06:30] Sofia (security): on fallback, we need to ensure keys and telemetry don't leak off VPC — if a request routes to hosted fallback is that allowed?
[06:38] Maya: for enterprise VPC/private we keep everything on VPC unless you opt into hosted burst. we can block hosted fallback for compliance. we noted your security doc request, we'll include that.

[07:05] Rajiv: back to quant accuracy — we saw a specific pattern where list-of-diagnosis lines were truncated or mis-tagged after scale events, could that be KV interleaving?
[07:16] Leo: possible — if prefix KV is missing or misapplied, the model loses context window so NER spans collapse. we'll correlate token-level timestamps with cache miss logs you supplied.

[08:00] Speaker 3 (generic): what microbenchmarks will you run for us?
[08:06] Leo: plan: 1) layer-sensitivity scan for int8/awq/gptq variants; 2) FP8 vs FP16 perf/accuracy run; 3) KV staleness stress test with controlled scale up/down events; 4) batching sensitivity sweep to measure tail p99 with different batch sizes and dynamic batching windows.
[08:28] Maya: we'll share raw logs and a reproducible infra recipe (Emulator script) so you can run locally.

[09:10] Elena: for KV staleness test, can you simulate our exact HPA behavior? our scale is aggressive, scales in ~15s steps.
[09:18] Priya: yes we can script that. also a note — workload burstiness is important: if you have caching hotspots the cold-start cost dominates.

[10:02] Tom: one anomaly: in one trace the model returned inconsistent entity labels but latency stayed normal, so it wasn't a cold start, what's the hypothesis?
[10:12] Leo: could be a partial KV mismatch (some layers read old KV pointers), or a quantization-path crossing where a few tokens were processed on a different precision path due to a misrouted request. we've seen routing race conditions where older requests slip to backup nodes with different model variants.
[10:33] Rajiv: is that a known bug in the runtime?
[10:36] Leo: it's an edge case, rare, often triggered by very tight autoscale windows plus a mixed-deploy config. Redwood patched a race in 2026-05, but customers with custom routing policies can still hit it if TTLs and sticky policies are misaligned.

[11:05] Maya: ok for mitigations: 1) short-term: enable sticky-KV + short TTL and set conservative HPA cooldown; 2) medium: run hybrid sensitivity and pin sensitive layers to FP16; 3) long-term: we can propose a canary comparator that checks entity-level F1 on a small prompt set and triggers rollback.
[11:28] Rajiv: sounds good. can you give us ballpark numbers on latency/throughput hit for hybrid strategy (some layers FP16, rest int8)?
[11:36] Leo: typical hit is 8-15% latency increase depending on which layers are kept in FP16; throughput drop around 10% but cost per token often still lower than full FP16 if you quantize the big attention matmuls.

[12:05] Elena: will need that spelled out for finance.
[12:08] Maya: we'll add an estimated cost table in the spreadsheet with perf numbers and expected resource delta.

[12:30] Tom: another ask: when you surface the layer-sensitivity results, can you annotate with suggested rollout order for canary? we want minimal blast radius.
[12:39] Leo: yes we will include per-layer suggested rollout: candidate first for cold-start safe layers, then head layers last. also provide a gating metric and sample prompts.

[13:05] Rajiv: final question on regression debugging — can Redwood produce diffs of token logits between baseline FP16 and candidate AWQ runs? we prefer per-token deltas.
[13:16] Maya: yes that's part of the regression kit, we can share delta tables and aggregated metrics.

[13:40] Wrap and next steps.
[13:42] Maya: recap - Redwood shares raw hybrid profiling sheet and emulator recipe by Friday, customer provides prompt set and infra metrics, Redwood runs microbench and returns recommended hybrid config and canary gating.
[13:56] Rajiv: we'll aim to get the prompt set and metrics early next week. thanks everyone.
